candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

'But you, who could not deceive my servant JOB — by honor I will inherit your throne to those of them; those whom you could not deceive, I will give the Kingdom of Heaven — says God who rules all.' Direct reference to JOB 1-2 — the prologue dialogue in which Satan attempts (with God's permission) to deceive Job through suffering and fails. The verse functions as GOD'S RESPONSE to the Devil's petition in Ch. 1: those whom the Devil could NOT deceive shall inherit his lost glory. Theological move: the Mäqabyan dialogue-form delivers what Augustine articulates in Enchiridion §29 + City of God 22.1 + Anselm Cur Deus Homo I.16-18 and Gregory the Great Homiliae in Evangelia 34 — the doctrine that THE NUMBER OF THE ELECT EQUALS THE NUMBER OF FALLEN ANGELS, and humans fill the empty seats. Meqabyan's distinctive contribution: the dialogue-form-delivery via the Devil's-own-petition.

candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

EXPANSION of Job-allusion (paired with seed 2:1 'But you, who could not deceive my servant JOB...'): the chapter develops Job's patient-suffering as PARADIGM for human-resistance-to-Devil's-deception. The Job-as-paradigm reading parallels: JAMES 5:11 ('Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy'); 1 CLEMENT 17 (Job alongside Abraham + Moses as faith-exemplars); BARUCH 3:30 (Job in the wisdom-tradition catalog); TESTAMENT OF JOB (an early-Jewish-Christian Job-haggadah from 1st c. BCE-CE; Schaller 1979). Patristic Job-as-Christ-typology readings: AMBROSE De Interpellatione Iob et David; CHRYSOSTOM Commentary on Job; GREGORY THE GREAT Moralia in Iob (the foundational Latin Job-commentary). Meqabyan's distinctive contribution: the Job-paradigm is DELIVERED VIA THE DEVIL'S DEFEAT — Job's victory is presented as evidence-against-the-Devil's-claim that humans can be deceived. Theological move: prosopopoeia of the Devil-as-defeated-petitioner.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

Theme of DIVINE-JUSTICE distinct from divine-permission: the verse develops the theological distinction between God permitting Satan-trial (Job 1:12 + 2:6) vs God authorizing Satan-defeat (Job 42:7-8 + 42:10). The permission-vs-defeat distinction parallels patristic theodicy: AUGUSTINE City of God 11.17 (God permits-but-does-not-author evil); JOHN OF DAMASCUS De Fide Orthodoxa 4.19-20 (the distinction between God's antecedent and consequent wills); MAXIMUS THE CONFESSOR Quaestiones ad Thalassium 1 (God permits Satan's rebellion to maximize-cosmic-good via greater-redemption); GREGORY NAZIANZEN Oration 31.15. Meqabyan's distinctive contribution: the permission-vs-defeat theological framework is delivered VIA THE DEVIL'S RECOGNITION of his own defeat — the structural irony of the Devil acknowledging God's-victory. Tewahedo theological reception reads 2:9 as the canonical proof-text for distinguishing PERMITTED-SUFFERING from authored-injustice.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

DIVINE-RESTORATION-OF-INHERITANCE — the verse's promise: those whom the Devil could not deceive shall INHERIT his lost-glory. Direct parallels to the angelic-replacement doctrine: AUGUSTINE Enchiridion §29 ('the empty places of the city of God may be filled up by the elect of the human race'); ANSELM Cur Deus Homo I.16-18 (the most extended single treatment — the elect-fill-the-angelic-vacancies); GREGORY THE GREAT Homiliae in Evangelia 34 (the lost-drachma + humans-replace-the-fallen-tenth doctrine — see seed 3 Mq 4:8 'tenth tribe'); THOMAS AQUINAS Summa Theologiae I.23.7 (the doctrine formalized scholastically). The angelic-replacement doctrine is preserved in EOTC Mäṣḥafä Mälaʾek (Book of the Angels) and integrated into Tewahedo angelological catechesis. The verse establishes the SOTERIOLOGICAL TELOS for the entire 3 Mq theological-anthropology systematic (Chs 4-10): humans are designed-to-replace-the-fallen-tenth, fulfilled-through-grace + complete-repentance.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

Theme of DIVINE-JUSTICE distinct from divine-permission: the verse develops the theological distinction between God permitting Satan-trial (Job 1:12 + 2:6) vs God authorizing Satan-defeat (Job 42:7-8 + 42:10). The permission-vs-defeat distinction parallels patristic theodicy: AUGUSTINE City of God 11.17 (God permits-but-does-not-author evil); JOHN OF DAMASCUS De Fide Orthodoxa 4.19-20 (the distinction between God's antecedent and consequent wills); MAXIMUS THE CONFESSOR Quaestiones ad Thalassium 1 (God permits Satan's rebellion to maximize-cosmic-good via greater-redemption); GREGORY NAZIANZEN Oration 31.15. Meqabyan's distinctive contribution: the permission-vs-defeat theological framework is delivered VIA THE DEVIL'S RECOGNITION of his own defeat — the structural irony of the Devil acknowledging God's-victory. Tewahedo theological reception reads 2:9 as the canonical proof-text for distinguishing PERMITTED-SUFFERING from authored-injustice.

DIVINE-RESTORATION-OF-INHERITANCE — the verse's promise: those whom the Devil could not deceive shall INHERIT his lost-glory. Direct parallels to the angelic-replacement doctrine: AUGUSTINE Enchiridion §29 ('the empty places of the city of God may be filled up by the elect of the human race'); ANSELM Cur Deus Homo I.16-18 (the most extended single treatment — the elect-fill-the-angelic-vacancies); GREGORY THE GREAT Homiliae in Evangelia 34 (the lost-drachma + humans-replace-the-fallen-tenth doctrine — see seed 3 Mq 4:8 'tenth tribe'); THOMAS AQUINAS Summa Theologiae I.23.7 (the doctrine formalized scholastically). The angelic-replacement doctrine is preserved in EOTC Mäṣḥafä Mälaʾek (Book of the Angels) and integrated into Tewahedo angelological catechesis. The verse establishes the SOTERIOLOGICAL TELOS for the entire 3 Mq theological-anthropology systematic (Chs 4-10): humans are designed-to-replace-the-fallen-tenth, fulfilled-through-grace + complete-repentance.
